subject: Vendor RFP: vulnerability evidence & SBOM formats
messages:
From: James Park <james.park@evergreenbank.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: procurement@evergreenbank.com
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Vendor RFP: vulnerability evidence & SBOM formats

Hi Irene,

Thanks for taking part in Evergreen Bank's vendor RFP. We're working through the security appendix and I have a few targeted questions specific to your vulnerability management evidence and SBOM delivery that weren't fully covered by the PDF in the RFP. Can you confirm the following items or point me to artifacts we can include in our security review?

1) SAST/DAST cadence and typical coverage: which codebases are scanned, build-stage vs CI, and whether developers get triage tickets.
2) Pen test cadence and whether you provide a redacted executive summary suitable for third-party review (PII removed).
3) Patch SLAs by severity (we'd like to see P0/P1/P2 targets and examples of historic remediation windows).
4) SBOM format(s) you produce (SPDX/CycloneDX), frequency, and whether you can provide a sample manifest for the inference runtime components.
5) Retention/archival policy for scan evidence, and whether you provide tamper-evident attestations (signed artifacts).

If it's easier we can take these on a short call. I'm copying procurement with the timeline: we hope to complete vendor technical due diligence by 31 May.

Attachments: EVG-RFP-section-3-vm-questions.pdf (your security team referenced this in the RFP)

Thanks,
James Park
Senior InfoSec Analyst
Evergreen Bank

Subject: Re: Vendor RFP: vulnerability evidence & SBOM formats

Hi James — thank you, and appreciate the clear list. I can answer high-level items now and Marissa/Stephanie will share the evidence set and specifics.

Quick answers up front:
- SAST/DAST: SAST runs in CI on every PR for our model-serving code and control plane repos; DAST runs weekly against staging and on-demand pre-release. We create developer tickets for confirmed findings (severity >= medium) and track through to closure.
- Pen tests: annual third-party penetration testing; we can provide a redacted executive summary suitable for vendor review.
- Patch SLAs: we have defined SLAs by severity; I'll ask Marissa to paste the table and historical examples.
- SBOM: we generate CycloneDX and SPDX manifests for release images; can provide a sample manifest for the inference runtime components.
- Retention & attestations: scan artifacts retained for 18 months by default; key artifacts are timestamped and signed using our internal artifact-signing service (we'll share process doc).

I'm attaching a short preliminary SAST summary and an SBOM sample to start. Would you be available for a 30m call Tues 19 May 10:00-10:30 PT? If that works I'll send a calendar invite and Marissa will join to cover SLA/patch examples.

Attachments: redwood_sast_summary_202605.pdf, sbom_sample_cyclonedx.xml

Best,

Hi James — following up with the operational detail you asked for. I'll summarize the key VM artifacts and SLAs below and attach the pen test executive summary (redacted). If you want specific CVE lists or the raw DAST report we can provide an on-demand export under an NDA.

Operational summary (concise):
1) SAST (static analysis)
   - Tooling: primary analysis with [internal SAST pipeline] + two commercial scanners during release gating.
   - Cadence: every PR (blocking for high findings), nightly full repo scan, and release-promoted scan.
   - Triage: findings are auto-filed to our issue tracker (severity mapping) and assigned to the owning team within 24 hours for high/critical ones.

2) DAST (dynamic analysis)
   - Scope: public control plane endpoints and staged internal-only endpoints used in pre-release testing.
   - Cadence: weekly automated runs + on-demand scans for major releases.
   - Findings: validated by our AppSec triage team; medium+ require remediation plan within 5 business days.

3) Penetration Testing
   - Cadence: annual, plus targetted tests for major infra changes (e.g., new GPU orchestration).
   - Deliverable: redacted executive summary and remediation timeline; full report available under stricter NDA.
   - Example: last test (Apr 2026) delivered a 6-page exec summary; high findings were mitigated within an average of 9 days (see attached summary).

4) Patch SLAs (target windows from discovery/triage)
   - P0 / Critical: 48 hours (hotfix pipeline, emergency rollout)
   - P1 / High: 7 calendar days (prioritized sprint/workaround then patch)
   - P2 / Medium: 30 calendar days
   - P3 / Low: next quarterly maintenance window
   - Historical evidence: we maintain an audit table; examples available in the evidence bundle (sample entries attached).

5) SBOMs and software component evidence
   - Formats produced: CycloneDX (primary) and SPDX (on request).
   - Granularity: per-release image manifests (layers and top-level packages) plus a runtime manifest for model-serving binary components.
   - Frequency: produced at each release and when reproducing images for incident investigations.

6) Evidence retention and attestations
   - Default retention: 18 months for scan artifacts and SBOM exports; critical incident artifacts retained longer on case-by-case basis.
   - Attestations: artifacts can be signed and time-stamped; we provide hash manifests and signature metadata for review.

Attachments included: pen_test-exec-summary_redacted.pdf, sample_evidence_audit_table.csv

Next steps:
- Please confirm the SBOM sample scope (container runtime components vs full build chain).
- We're happy to host an evidence review session under your NDA.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Head of Security Operations
